Copy ADB command for advanced mode

Android has no public way for apps to switch NFC, so by default Able, its NFC tile and widget open Android's NFC settings.

Advanced mode switches NFC directly. Grant "Write secure settings" once from a computer with ADB:

%1$s

The same permission lets Able switch USB/wireless debugging and Private DNS. With Shizuku connected, Able grants itself this permission the first time you use one of these switches, and tells you. To undo, run the same command with "revoke" instead of "grant", or uninstall Able.

Advanced mode follows the open-source "NFC Quick Settings" app by Paul Colby.
Shizuku is connected: on first use Able grants itself \"Write secure settings\", then changes these settings directly and checks the result.
Able used Shizuku to grant itself \"Write secure settings\": these settings change directly, also from tiles and widgets.

Able used Shizuku to grant itself "Write secure settings" (the same permission the ADB command grants). It lets Able switch NFC, USB/wireless debugging and Private DNS directly, and stays granted even when Shizuku stops. The grant is recorded in the action history.
